q: By how much does a $25\,\text{m}$ long copper pipe get longer when it warms up from $10\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ to $60\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ ($\alpha = 17 \cdot 10^{-6}\,\tfrac{1}{\text{K}}$)?
a: $\Delta L = \alpha L_0 \Delta T = 17 \cdot 10^{-6}\,\tfrac{1}{\text{K}} \cdot 25\,\text{m} \cdot 50\,\text{K} \approx 0.021\,\text{m}$, that is, about 21 mm.
